Container.Name: Hearth
Container.Overview:
A self-hosted personal relationship manager: the people in your life, how they are related, what you gave them, and where you saw them — with one-way sync out to Google Contacts and Google Calendar so it all shows up on your phone.
REQUIRES A POSTGRES 16 CONTAINER. Install PostgreSQL 16 from Community Applications first, create a database for Hearth, and put its connection string in DATABASE_URL below. Hearth stores everything — including contact photos — in that database, so it is the only thing you need to back up.
ALSO REQUIRES A GOOGLE OAUTH CLIENT, which takes about ten minutes to create and is free. Hearth cannot ship a shared one: Google requires an app to list the exact address it is used from, and yours is unique to you. The upside is that your app has one user and never needs Google's review. Full walkthrough: docs/google-setup.md in the project repository.
Set HEARTH_ALLOWED_EMAILS before first start if this is reachable from the internet. Until the install has a user, the first person to sign in claims it.
Everything else is optional and off by default. There is no telemetry and no Hearth server: the only remote service involved is Google.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port Hearth listens on. Put a reverse proxy in front of it if you are exposing it to the internet — Hearth expects to be reached over https.

Config.Name: DATABASE_URL
Config.Description: Connection string for your Postgres 16 container. Use the server's LAN IP rather than localhost — a bridged container cannot reach another container that way. Create the database and user in Postgres first.

Config.Name: AUTH_URL
Config.Description: The address you reach Hearth at, with https and NO trailing slash. Must match the redirect URI in your Google OAuth client exactly — a mismatch here is the most common reason sign-in fails.

Config.Name: AUTH_SECRET
Config.Description: Session signing key. Generate one with: openssl rand -base64 32. Changing it signs everybody out.

Config.Name: AUTH_GOOGLE_ID
Config.Description: Client ID from your Google OAuth client. See docs/google-setup.md.

Config.Name: AUTH_GOOGLE_SECRET
Config.Description: Client secret from your Google OAuth client. Google shows it once.

Config.Name: HEARTH_ALLOWED_EMAILS
Config.Description: Who may sign in: email addresses, or @domain for anyone at a domain, comma-separated. Somebody who already has an account can always sign in, and while the install has no users at all the first sign-in claims it — so SET THIS BEFORE FIRST START if Hearth is reachable from the internet.

Config.Name: AUTH_TRUST_HOST
Config.Description: Leave as true when running behind a reverse proxy, which on Unraid you almost certainly are.

Config.Name: SYNC_ENABLED
Config.Description: Background sync to Google. Set false to stop the timer; the Sync now buttons still work.

Config.Name: SYNC_INTERVAL_SECONDS
Config.Description: How often background sync runs. Minimum 30.

Config.Name: HEARTH_ENABLE_MAIL
Config.Description: Set true to let Hearth email thank-you notes as you. Off by default because it needs a Gmail scope most installs never use — and you must reconnect Google after switching it on.

Config.Name: GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY
Config.Description: Optional. Better address and venue lookup for event locations. Without it Hearth uses OpenStreetMap, which needs no key.

Config.Name: OLLAMA_URL
Config.Description: Optional. A model on your own network, e.g. http://192.168.1.10:11434 — enables typing a search in plain words, and searching contacts by meaning. Install Ollama from Community Applications and pull qwen2.5:7b-instruct and nomic-embed-text. Unset means neither feature is offered.

Config.Name: OLLAMA_EMBED_MODEL
Config.Description: Optional. Default nomic-embed-text. Changing it re-indexes every contact.

Config.Name: HEARTH_SOURCE_URL
Config.Description: Optional. Where to get this install's source, offered in the footer because the AGPL asks for it. Set it only if you have modified Hearth; leave blank to point at the upstream project.
